terms: Academic Learning & Achievement What young people learn and how they progress through school: demonstrated learning by subject, the behaviors and beliefs that shape learning, and school and postsecondary status. All academic outcomes live here, in three categories.

Literacy: Reading & Writing Literacy Subject learning A demonstrated gain in reading (phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension, reading level) or in writing and composition in any genre. Reading level, fluency, comprehension scores; reading or ELA test proficiency; writing quality, essays, published writing presented as a writing skill.

English Language Development & Multilingualism English language development Subject learning Growth in English proficiency for English learners (listening, speaking, reading, writing), or maintenance and development of a home language alongside English. ELP level gains, reclassification, WIDA/ELPAC-type scores; bilingual or home-language maintenance for youth.

Mathematics Mathematics Subject learning A demonstrated gain in math skill, problem-solving or grade-level math proficiency. Math test scores and proficiency; specific math skills; math used in money contexts when the outcome is the math.

Science, Technology & Engineering Science, technology & engineering Subject learning A demonstrated gain in science (life, physical, earth, environmental), engineering design, or computing and coding, including digital-literacy skills. Science test proficiency; ecosystem or ecology knowledge; engineering design process; coding, computational thinking, digital skills.

Other Academic Subjects Other academic subjects Subject learning A demonstrated gain in history, geography, economics, world languages or another academic subject not covered by Y1.1-Y1.4 or Y1.6. History and geography content; economics concepts; a world language learned by a native English speaker; other ESSA well-rounded subjects.

Arts Learning Arts learning Subject learning A demonstrated gain in technique, vocabulary or knowledge of an art form (dance, media arts, music, theatre, visual arts). Instrument proficiency; dance or art vocabulary; juried or assessed artistic skill.

Critical Thinking, Inquiry & Media Literacy Critical thinking & media literacy Subject learning Analyzing and evaluating information and sources, research and inquiry skills, and media literacy, in any subject. Evaluating source credibility; identifying misinformation; research projects framed as inquiry skill; analyzing conflicting sources.

Early Learning & School Readiness Early learning & school readiness Subject learning Early language, literacy, math and cognitive development, and kindergarten readiness, for children below kindergarten age. Pre-literacy (letter recognition, phonemic awareness); early numeracy; readiness assessments; broad developmental milestones on screeners such as the ASQ.

Academic Engagement Behaviors Academic engagement behaviors Learning behaviors & mindsets Observable participation in schoolwork: homework completion, being prepared, class participation. Homework completion rates; asking questions and taking part in class discussions; coming prepared.

Academic Perseverance Academic perseverance Learning behaviors & mindsets Sticking with difficult schoolwork or learning tasks despite setbacks, including task persistence in young children. Persisting on hard problems; not giving up on assignments; early-childhood task persistence.

Learning Strategies & Study Skills Learning strategies Learning behaviors & mindsets Using specific methods to learn: note-taking, planners, test preparation, self-quizzing, metacognition. Named study techniques; planning schoolwork with a tool.

Academic Mindsets & Self-Efficacy Academic mindsets Learning behaviors & mindsets Beliefs about oneself as a learner: academic self-efficacy, belonging in academic work, and growth mindset about intelligence or ability to learn. 'I can succeed in this class'; believing intelligence or math ability grows with effort; confidence in academic abilities.

Attendance & School Stability Attendance & school stability Educational progress & attainment A student's school attendance, chronic absence, or staying enrolled in school through disruption (homelessness, foster placement changes, pregnancy). Attendance rates for participating students; chronic absenteeism; remaining enrolled or in the school of origin.

Exclusionary Discipline Exclusionary discipline Educational progress & attainment Suspensions, expulsions, office discipline referrals, and alternatives that replace them. Fewer suspensions or referrals; restorative alternatives to suspension; school-level suspension rates.

Grades, Credits & On-Track Status Grades, credits & on-track Educational progress & attainment Course grades, GPA, course passing, credit accumulation, promotion, 9th-grade on-track status, and 'academic performance' or test scores with no subject named. GPA; passing core classes; credits for promotion; unspecified academic achievement.

Advanced Coursework & Dual Credit Advanced coursework Educational progress & attainment Enrolling in or completing advanced courses: AP, IB, honors, advanced STEM electives, dual enrollment and college credit earned in high school. AP/IB/honors enrollment; dual enrollment; college credit before graduation.

High School Completion & Re-engagement High school completion Educational progress & attainment Graduating from high school, earning a GED or equivalency, or re-enrolling after leaving school. On-time graduation; GED; re-engagement after dropout or release.

Postsecondary Enrollment, Persistence & Completion Postsecondary enrollment & completion Educational progress & attainment Enrolling in, persisting in, or completing college or other postsecondary education or training after high school. College enrollment the fall after graduation; first-to-second-year persistence; degree or certificate completion.

Engagement, Interest & Creative Expression How young people experience learning and activities: enjoyment, curiosity, lasting interest, seeing relevance, creative expression, and choosing to take part.

Enjoyment & Joy Enjoyment Enjoyment & interest A positive emotional experience of the program or of learning: fun, happiness, excitement, pride in being part of it. Reports of enjoying activities; excitement to attend; pride in the program.

Curiosity & Triggered Interest Curiosity Enjoyment & interest Interest sparked in the moment: curiosity, asking questions about something new, willingness to try a new activity. Asking questions during a demonstration; trying new activities; showing curiosity.

Sustained & Individual Interest Sustained interest Enjoyment & interest Interest that persists, deepens or becomes the young person's own: a passion, returning to a topic, pursuing it beyond the program. Discovering a passion; continuing an activity after the program; self-directed pursuit of a topic.

Relevance & Utility Value Relevance & utility value Enjoyment & interest Seeing learning as useful for one's goals, future plans or community. Explaining how a subject connects to careers or daily life; valuing what is learned.

Creative Expression & Performance Creative expression & performance Expression & participation Self-expression through making something (art, music, writing, design), presenting or performing finished work, or responding to art, as an experience rather than a stated skill gain. Composing, creating, exhibiting, performing, critiquing or connecting art to personal meaning.

Participation in Enriching Activities Participation in activities Expression & participation An individual young person's choice to take part in constructive activities, inside the program (returning, joining) or outside it (sports, arts, clubs, faith groups). Returning for another year; joining a team or club; participating fully alongside peers; per-person participation thresholds.
Belonging & Relationships The relationships around a young person: belonging, supportive adults, friends, family, and wider networks.

Belonging & Mattering Belonging Connectedness Feeling accepted, valued, included and safe in the program, school or a community; mattering; less isolation. Sense of belonging; feeling safe and accepted in program spaces; feeling connected to a new community; reduced loneliness.

Supportive Adult Relationships Supportive adults Close relationships A caring, trusting relationship with at least one adult outside the family (mentor, staff, teacher, coach), including its quality (care, challenge, support). Naming a trusted adult; a mentor who cares or challenges; permanent adult connections for youth in care.
Peer Relationships & Friendship Peer relationships Close relationships Friendships, peer acceptance and a positive peer group. Making friends; a supportive peer community; friendships across groups.

Family Relationships Family relationships Close relationships The young person's own relationship with their family: communication, connection, repair, reunification. Reunification; rebuilding trust with family; better communication with parents as described from the youth side.

Social Capital & Networks Social capital & networks Networks Access to, and use of, a wider network of relationships (adults, peers, professionals, employers) that can open educational or career opportunities. Expanding a professional network; introductions and references; contacts who can help with a goal.
Social & Emotional Skills (CASEL) Social and emotional skills: what young people can do, organized by CASEL's five competencies. Beliefs about oneself are in Y5.
Emotion Awareness Emotion awareness Self-awareness Recognizing and naming one's own emotions. Identifying feelings; using a feelings chart; naming emotions in hard moments.

Emotion Regulation & Coping Emotion regulation & coping Self-management Managing strong emotions and impulses, and using coping strategies for stress, worry or frustration. Calming down; frustration tolerance; self-regulation; deep breathing or journaling to manage stress.

Goal-Setting, Organization & Self-Discipline Goals & self-discipline Self-management Setting personal goals and working toward them, and general organization, self-discipline and persistence outside schoolwork. Setting and pursuing goals; completing projects; keeping materials organized; follow-through.

Empathy, Perspective-Taking & Social Awareness Empathy & social awareness Social awareness Understanding and caring about others' feelings and perspectives, expressing gratitude, and reading social norms and expectations in different settings. Perspective-taking; compassion; gratitude; understanding expectations in class, online and community settings.

Respect for Diversity & Cultural Competence Respect for diversity Social awareness Respecting and including people of different backgrounds and identities, and examining one's own biases. Respect for peers of other cultures, religions, abilities; inclusive behavior; bias awareness.

Communication & Public Speaking Communication & public speaking Relationship skills Expressing oneself clearly, listening actively, and speaking to an audience. Active listening; clear communication; presentations and public speaking.

Teamwork, Collaboration & Group Leadership Teamwork & group leadership Relationship skills Working with others toward shared goals, including leading peers within a group task. Collaboration on projects; teamwork; taking turns leading a small group; leadership within a team activity.

Relationship-Building & Conflict Resolution Relationships & conflict resolution Relationship skills Building, maintaining and repairing relationships, and resolving interpersonal conflict constructively. Resolving disagreements without fighting; de-escalation; repairing a friendship.

Help-Seeking & Offering Support Help-seeking Relationship skills Knowing where to find support, asking for help, and offering help to others. Willingness to seek help; naming resources to contact in a crisis; helping peers.

Decision-Making & Problem-Solving Decision-making & problem-solving Responsible decision-making Weighing options and consequences and working a personal or social problem through from identifying it to acting. Pros and cons before a decision; structured problem-solving; anticipating consequences.

Ethical & Prosocial Choices Ethical & prosocial choices Responsible decision-making Making an ethical or prosocial choice in a specific situation, including small daily contributions to the class or program. Reporting bullying instead of joining in; standing up for a classmate; helping clean up the space.

Risk Avoidance & Refusal Skills Risk avoidance & refusal Responsible decision-making Avoiding unsafe situations and resisting negative peer pressure. Refusal skills; leaving unsafe situations; resisting pressure to use substances.
Identity, Confidence & Agency Who young people believe they are and what they believe they can do: identity, confidence, purpose and agency.

Self-Understanding & Identity Exploration Self-understanding Identity Understanding who one is, what matters to one, and how one is changing. Identity exploration; articulating one's values and experiences.

Cultural & Social Identity Cultural & social identity Identity Pride in, and acceptance of, one's own cultural, ethnic, linguistic, gender, sexual or other social identity. Pride in heritage; self-acceptance of sexual orientation or gender identity; bicultural identity.

Domain Identity Domain identity Identity Seeing oneself as a certain kind of person in a field: 'a STEM person', an artist, an athlete, a reader, a writer. 'See themselves as' statements tied to a field.

Confidence, Self-Efficacy & Self-Worth Confidence & self-worth Self-beliefs A general belief that one can succeed and handle challenges, including general growth mindset and self-esteem. Self-confidence; self-efficacy; self-esteem; naming one's strengths; growth mindset about setbacks.

Purpose & Future Orientation Purpose & future orientation Purpose & agency A sense of purpose and meaning, optimism about the future, and aspirations, including spiritual purpose and growth in faith. Sense of purpose; hopes and goals for life; growth in faith or spiritual life.

Agency, Self-Determination & Self-Advocacy Agency & self-advocacy Purpose & agency Acting as the causal agent in one's own life: making choices, advocating for one's own needs, directing one's own supports. Self-advocacy in IEP meetings; leading one's own IEP; requesting accommodations; making and explaining one's own choices.

Character, Values & Civic Life How young people relate to their community and its systems: values, civic knowledge, critical consciousness, civic action, environmental stewardship and digital citizenship.

Positive Values & Character Values & character Character General character traits and guiding values: integrity, honesty, responsibility, sportsmanship, forgiveness, faith-grounded values. Honesty; responsibility; sportsmanship; living out values, including faith-based values.

Civic Knowledge Civic knowledge Civic understanding Understanding how government, civic institutions, elections and rights work. How a bill becomes law; branches of government; how the school board decides; voter registration process.

Critical Consciousness & Social Justice Critical consciousness Civic understanding Analyzing power, inequity and systems of oppression, and acting against injustice. Analyzing why food deserts or zoning inequality exist; articulating how systemic racism affects a community.

Civic Voice, Leadership & Participation Civic voice & participation Civic action Influencing collective decisions and taking part in civic life: youth councils, testimony, advocacy, co-design, organizing, voting, and civic efficacy. Presenting to a city council; youth advisory boards; organizing campaigns; registering and voting; believing one can influence community decisions.

Community Service & Action Community service & action Civic action Organized service or projects to improve the community, including identifying a community issue and planning action on it. Service hours; service trips; food drives; community action plans.

Environmental Stewardship Environmental stewardship Civic action Caring for the environment and acting on it: pro-environmental behavior and connection to nature. Recycling and composting; reducing waste; stewardship; connection to nature.

Digital Citizenship & Online Safety Digital citizenship Digital citizenship Safe, legal and ethical behavior online: privacy, security, recognizing scams, respectful conduct. Protecting personal information; strong passwords; recognizing phishing.

Career & Economic Readiness Readiness for and results in work and independent adult life: career exploration, transition steps, work skills, credentials, employment, money skills and daily living skills.

Career Awareness & Exploration Career exploration Exploration & navigation Learning about careers and pathways, interest inventories, workplace and campus visits, and interest in or aspiration toward a career field. Researching careers; exploring pathways; interest in a STEM career; college visits.

College & Career Transition Knowledge Transition knowledge Exploration & navigation Knowing and completing the process of moving to college or work: applications, FAFSA, financial aid, resumes, interviews. FAFSA completion; college applications; comparing aid letters; resume writing.

Employability & Workplace Skills Employability skills Work readiness Professionalism and workplace skills: punctuality, workplace communication, initiative, job performance. Professional conduct; supervisor evaluations; workplace communication.

Technical Skills, Credentials & Work-Based Learning Technical skills & credentials Work readiness Industry-specific skills, recognized credentials and certifications, and completing internships or apprenticeships. Industry certifications; apprenticeship completion; trade skills.

Employment & Earnings Employment & earnings Employment & independence Getting or keeping a job, wages and earnings, and combined 'employed or in education' indicators. Job placement; paid work hours; wages; competitive integrated employment; WIOA-style combined indicators.

Financial Capability Financial capability Employment & independence The young person's own financial knowledge, habits and decisions: budgeting, saving, banking, credit, understanding pay and taxes. Budgets; savings accounts; reading a pay stub; understanding credit and interest.

Independent Living Skills Independent living skills Employment & independence Daily living skills for self-sufficiency: cooking, scheduling, transportation, self-care away from home, and obtaining vital documents. Independent-living skill bundles; getting an ID, Social Security card and birth certificate; self-care at camp.

Health, Safety & Well-Being A young person's own health and safety: daily health habits, motor skills, health knowledge, sexual health and health care; mental health; felt safety, risk behavior and justice involvement.

Healthy Daily Habits Healthy daily habits Physical health Everyday health behaviors: physical activity and fitness, nutrition and healthy eating, sleep, hygiene, and recreational screen time. Minutes of activity; fitness; fruit and vegetable intake; healthy cooking framed as nutrition; hours of sleep; handwashing; less screen time.

Motor & Sport Skills Motor & sport skills Physical health Fundamental movement, fine and gross motor, and sport-specific or outdoor physical skills. Dribbling and passing; swimming levels; running, jumping, throwing; fine motor skills; hiking or climbing technique.

Health Knowledge & Safety Skills Health knowledge & safety skills Physical health Health information and safety skills not covered by another health code: first aid, injury prevention, finding reliable health information, and health education content. First aid; outdoor safety; health class content; how to respond to an allergic reaction.

Sexual & Reproductive Health Sexual & reproductive health Physical health Knowledge and behavior related to sexual health, STI and pregnancy prevention, and healthy relationships in that context. STI prevention knowledge; delaying pregnancy; accessing confidential services.

Health Care Access & Condition Management Health care access Physical health Getting and using health care: insurance, preventive and dental or vision visits, screenings, immunizations, and managing chronic conditions. Enrolling in insurance; annual screenings; developmental screenings received; asthma self-management.

Mental Health Symptoms & Distress Mental health symptoms Mental health Fewer symptoms of anxiety, depression, distress or behavioral problems in the young person. Lower anxiety or depression scores; fewer outbursts; less self-reported stress.
Flourishing & Life Satisfaction Flourishing Mental health Positive mental health: life satisfaction, flourishing, feeling restored or well. Life satisfaction; flourishing; general well-being.

Healing & Trauma Recovery Trauma recovery Mental health A young person processing trauma, feeling psychologically safe during recovery, and moving toward healing. Processing traumatic events; psychological safety for trauma-exposed youth.

Mental Health Service Access & Use Mental health service use Mental health Being connected to and using counseling, therapy or crisis services. Referrals completed; sessions attended; connection to community providers.
Felt Safety Felt safety Safety, risk & justice Feeling safe at home, at school or in the neighborhood, not specific to the program. Feeling safe walking to school or in the neighborhood.

Substance Use Substance use Safety, risk & justice Use, intentions or perceived risk of tobacco, vaping, alcohol or other drugs. Reduced use; delayed first use; lower intentions; higher perceived risk; knowledge of risks.

Violence, Bullying & Victimization Violence & victimization Safety, risk & justice Fighting, weapon carrying, bullying, harassment, dating violence and community violence, as perpetrator or victim. Fewer fights; less weapon carrying; less harassment; dating-violence warning signs.

Justice Involvement, Diversion & Reentry Justice involvement Safety, risk & justice Avoiding justice-system involvement, completing diversion or probation, and reduced recidivism. No new adjudication; completing a restorative agreement; avoiding re-arrest.

Family & Caregiver Strengthening Caregivers and other adult participants: parenting and home learning, caregiver well-being and connections, adult education and system navigation, and the family's partnership with the program.

Parenting Knowledge & Practices Parenting Parenting & home learning Caregivers' child-development knowledge, parenting practices, parent-child interaction and parenting confidence, including teen parents. Knowledge of milestones; positive discipline; positive interactions; parenting confidence.

Home Learning Environment & Routines Home learning Parenting & home learning Family practices that support a child's learning and development at home: reading together, routines, homework time. Reading at home; bedtime and daily routines; homework space.

Family Health Practices Family health practices Parenting & home learning Caregiver or household health practices for children: breastfeeding, safe sleep, well-child visits kept by the parent, family eating habits. Breastfeeding; safe sleep; well-child visits; family fruit and vegetable intake.

Caregiver Well-Being & Resilience Caregiver well-being Caregiver well-being & support The caregiver's own stress, mental health and resilience. Reduced parenting stress; lower caregiver depression; resilience.

Caregiver Social Connections Caregiver connections Caregiver well-being & support Caregivers building supportive relationships with other parents or their community. Parent friendships; peer support groups.

Adult Education, Skills & Employment Adult education & employment Adult development & navigation The education, training, English proficiency, digital or financial skills, and employment of a caregiver or other adult participant. GED or job training for parents; adult ESL; digital literacy for family members or older adults.

System Navigation & Rights Knowledge Navigation & rights Adult development & navigation Families knowing their rights, knowing where to turn for help, navigating school or service systems, and getting connected to resources. IDEA rights knowledge; understanding enrollment and health systems; connecting to resources; knowing where to turn in a crisis.

Family Connection & Trust with the Program Family-program trust Family-program partnership The family's relationship with and trust in the program or school, and communication between them. Families feeling welcome; trust in staff; feeling connected to the school community.

Family Participation & Leadership Family participation & leadership Family-program partnership Families attending, volunteering or taking part in program or school decisions. Serving on advisory councils; attending workshops (per-family thresholds); volunteering.
Basic Needs & Economic Stability The material stability of a household or of a young person living independently: income and benefits, food, housing.

Income, Benefits & Financial Stability Income & benefits Economic stability Household or independent-youth income, public benefits, and financial stability. Household income; SNAP/TANF/Medicaid enrollment; household savings.
Food Security Food security Food & housing Having enough food and access to healthy food. Reduced food insecurity; fewer skipped meals; less reliance on emergency food.

Housing Stability & Safe Living Situation Housing stability Food & housing Securing or keeping safe, stable housing, for a household or a young person living independently. Exits to stable housing; avoiding eviction; keeping a lease; reduced rent burden.
Staff & Volunteer Capacity The adults who serve young people: what they learn, what they change in practice, and whether the workforce is stable and well.

Staff & Volunteer Knowledge & Skills Staff learning Staff learning & practice Staff, volunteers, mentors, coaches or case managers gaining knowledge or skills. Training outcomes; staff confidence; volunteers' understanding.

Practice Change Practice change Staff learning & practice Adults applying new practices, including trauma-informed care. Implementing a curriculum or screener; adopting restorative or trauma-informed practice.
Workforce Stability & Well-Being Workforce stability Workforce Staff retention and turnover, and staff well-being. Turnover rates; retention; burnout.
Program Quality, Access & Reach The program itself: quality, satisfaction, access and inclusion, reach and dosage (outputs), and systems for engaging families.

Program Quality Program quality Quality & experience Observed or assessed program quality (safe, supportive, interactive, engaging environment) and accreditation. YPQA or similar scores; accreditation; a more welcoming or affirming environment.

Participant & Family Satisfaction Satisfaction Quality & experience Participants' or families' satisfaction with the program and their perceptions of its quality and safety. Satisfaction ratings; parents' confidence in program safety.

Access to Resources Access to resources Access & inclusion Providing materials, devices, connectivity or facilities, including counts of resources distributed. Laptops and hotspots; home internet; facilities access.

Inclusion, Accommodations & Language Access Inclusion & language access Access & inclusion Removing barriers so that all participants can take part: accommodations, accessible formats, interpretation and translation. Sensory kits and visual schedules; accessible materials; interpreters; home-language communications.

Participation, Dosage & Reach (Output) Participation & reach (output) Reach & engagement systems Program-level counts, rates and dosage: youth served, attendance rates, sessions, match length, training hours, and services staff delivered. Number served; average daily attendance; match duration; sessions delivered; applications submitted by staff.

Family Engagement Systems Family engagement systems Reach & engagement systems The organization's systems, events or policies for engaging families. Creating a parent advisory council; family engagement policies; family events offered.
Systems, Policy & Community Conditions Change beyond one program: policy and institutions, cross-sector partnerships, and community conditions.

Policy & Institutional Change Policy & institutional change Policy & institutions Changes to policy, funding or institutional practice in schools, districts, cities or states. New ordinances; district policies; dedicated budget funding.

Cross-Sector Partnerships Partnerships Partnerships & community Shared agendas, shared measurement and coordinated partnerships across organizations and sectors. Data-sharing agreements; shared data systems; coalition collaboration.

Community Conditions & Collective Efficacy Collective efficacy Partnerships & community Neighborhood cohesion, trust and willingness to act for the common good. Residents' trust; willingness to intervene for youth safety.
